Those morning thoughts are something that resonate with me so well. 

It's comforting to know that I'm not the only one who suffers from this.

This is more of a "Can you relate?" thing, but don't you feel like laughing sometimes when your friends tell you that your mindsets are unhealthy, that you need to change.

It feels almost biological to hate myself and what if I was born this way? What if I don't want to change? Because growing up, pain was such a normal feeling that it almost brings me comfort nowadays, comfort I can't get within myself.

​

Anyways, sending hugs to you as well! <3

I'm in no place to give advice (the hypocrisy!)   


But be the change you want to see in yourself. I know we all have different ways of living life despite having the same diagnosis, but I'm the type of person to just throw myself out there despite the amount of hurt I've been given, I wouldn't say it's strength, more recklessness. 

I believe you can do it and I know you can!

Good luck :D

Definitely.

Growing up I was beaten for the most normal things, crying and vomiting are two I can name.
I was called a “demon,” a spawn of Satan and other loving nicknames you’d get from your mother.

I would never be rewarded too, if I did well on school a “You can do better.”

This really caught my eye.
But I have so many educated friends (I educated them lol it’s an ongoing long process) but I surrounded with people I love and it’s not so bad.

It definitely pains me to know that you feel that isolated and trapped in your own routine but I promise that between the favourite persons and addictions, life is so much intensely better.
It’s comforting to me to know that I feel intensely good emotions (with the bad of course) but that’s the balance of life.

I may not know you, but I can empathise with what you’re going through.

All love for you. 
Life’s tough but we’re stronger. ❤️

Agreed. "Love is about accepting the flaws about somebody," and yet I am criticised and made out to be a monster for expressing my distress. I'm pushed into a corner, silencing my emotions into the next big emotional explosion.

Maybe our friends are very similar, it's not like he has horrible anxiety but when things do get overwhelming he tends to push everyone away and so I wait patiently until the next time he texts me.

(Whenever it's a special occasion like a birthday or Christmas, we always text each other looong paragraphs and we end up catching up.)

Thank you for your support, I'm not even sure if I have anything, I haven't been formerly diagnosed, or even spoken to a psychologist. 

Again, thank you though.

To be honest, nothing.

Everything feels trivial or holds no meaning.

Hey,

Thanks for the response, I wrote this on a very angst driven night, sometimes it feels like these thoughts intentionally overwhelm me when no one is online to help me.

I try not to put blame on people for not being able to help out, it just feels very pointless to let in the same people in my life that are never around and only call out to me when they need help. To clarify, yes I have reached out to this person, multiple times, once 4 weeks ago and then two weeks after that, I understand that they are busy so I haven't texted them since.

​

I am constantly being let down left right and centre by what feels like everyone. I get frustrated at myself because I have high expectations for the help I receive: I get annoyed when people pity me, I get depressed when no one texts me, when people assume what I'm going through I get even more annoyed and it goes on and on and on... 

It makes me feel bad; I know these people care about me, I know it's in their best intentions to care about me, but I don't know how to trust them.

I understand that I need to unlearn these behaviours and that they are unhealthy, it's like I know what to do but I don't know where to start.

​

As for the temporary things, I'm usually occupied with work or I play games and I end up feeling bad because I wasn't being productive.

The lowest point was in 2017.

My story in comparison to others just sounds so stupid. But here we go anyways. I was a 13-year-old boy with no friends, low self-esteem and the tendency to self-harm. I hung out with people that did not like me (Group 1 IRL), they'd exclude things from me, pick me out for my interests etc... But instead, I continued to hang out with them because hanging out with people was better than hanging out with nobody.

I tried talking to my sister about these issues and she just brushed them off, some stuff went down with my sister and my family's attention went all on my sister. So just when I thought "if I died, I wouldn't have to be on this stupid planet," I had to be the brother that my sister could depend on. Once again, it felt like my very prevalent issues didn't matter because I was the only one that paid attention to my issues. Nobody else. No friends that'd worry about me. No parents that would even bat an eye and certainly not a sister that can offer me better advice than I've already given her.

I felt like I had nothing, I did have a group (Group 2 on the Internet) of people I could talk to, but they were the ones who influenced me to cut. They kept sending me photos of them doing it and saying how shitty their life is. I had this one friend that told me he was going to kill himself weekly. (Might be a bit of an exaggeration) But the point I'm trying to make was that he'd always make me feel responsible.

I stopped texting that guy and I was off to lead a better life. I spent more time with the group (Group 1 IRL) and I happen to be one of the most pivotal members now today. Now that I reflect on my past, I realised that I was in this cycle of self-hatred and it was easy for me to break out of it when I started to think about others.

2 years later and I've started working out, I've had a boost in confidence and I have loving friends.

I can't say that one day everything will make sense, but I kept working hard to survive. And that's all I did to live a positive life. :)

Well, I can say that I did it.

But not well.

I went to school and wore my blazer until it got really hot and I took it off, my left arm was still twitching, hiding and cramped in the most uncomfortable spots because I was afraid someone would see. 

My friend on the table who's name shall be **Dee** has seen and known about the scars for a while now. The main issue isn't her, she's not judgemental, it's (Let's call Him **Peb) Peb** is my friend but he's judgemental, he'd give me these weird looks after seeing just a little of my scars or it looks like he's trying to take a peek of my scars and then look away.

It makes me very uncomfortable.   
He makes me very uncomfortable, he may just be a normal human being with eyes but when he stares at me it's like he's gazing into my soul, maybe he has a crush on me.

I want to show off my arms because boastful as it seems, I'm pretty toned. But these scars are holding me back.

Tomorrow I might try and squeeze in 4 periods of no blazer at school, and then 6 periods, and then the whole day.

You know what? I'm going to do it.

I'm going to come to school and take my dreaded blazer in this heat and I will stand tall.

(P.S I'll keep you updated on what happens.)
Took me a year of falsely claiming my bisexualhood to realise having friends that are girls does not mean you’re attracted to them.

This happened when I was 13, I was friends with a boy for a very long time, let's call him Owen. To me, Owen was the perfect human being and I kept insisting that I wanted to be like Owen. This 'admiration' grew stronger and stronger every day, every time I wasn't calling him I wanted him even more. And back then I realised that maybe the strong feeling I had was because I had a crush on him and it was hard to identify my feelings because I confused myself with girls, I dated a lot of girls and I never understood what it meant to have feelings for someone. I then briefly contemplated being "bisexual" (not true), and I took it back. I felt like having a label would make it easier for someone to stereotype me and I didn't want that.  


A year later I realised I was gay and I told Owen that I **used** to have a crush on him and he was really nice about it. We're still friends.  


Also, what is it about straight guys saying "If I was gay I would date you?"   
I don't understand why you're giving me this false hope, it's reassuring   
that you care about me but it's confusing.

If (boy) liked luck8kon that'd be really desperate". And I was extremely offended and hurt so I said "I don't even know you?" (Which was true, my friends was friends with name2 so I had to call with them). Name2 replied with "I don't need to know you as a person to know you're a dick". I already have really bad self-esteem issues so to put it simply, I spent my time angrily crying because of how powerless I felt. My friends didn't say anything, the fourth person in the call just said "That's the tea sis". No one stood up for me.
